headline_marked: [[Cabinet approves 9th national pay scale]], salaries to rise 100-142% for govt employees
headline: Cabinet approves 9th national pay scale, salaries to rise 100-142% for govt employees
summary: The new pay scale, retrospectively effective from July 1, will benefit approximately 2.4 million civilian government employees and 9.25 lakh pensioners. Its implementation will cost the government an estimated Tk 1.05 trillion annually.
details: The Cabinet has approved the new national pay scale for civilian government employees, increasing salaries, allowances, and pensions. It also approved a joint forces directive for the armed forces, with a separate structure for the judiciary to follow. All provisions are retrospectively effective from July 1.

Approved during a Cabinet meeting chaired by the Prime Minister, the new structure will see basic salaries rise by 100 to 142 percent across different grades. However, the disbursement of the increased salaries will occur in three phases over two fiscal years, starting from July 2026.

The decision followed reports from the National Pay Commission-2025 and the Armed Forces Pay Committee-2025, which were then reviewed by a Secretary Committee. The Cabinet considered this committee's recommendations.

Factors influencing the approval included the government's financial capacity, the country's overall economic situation, inflation, cost of living, the welfare of government employees, and the need for a balanced and rational pay structure.
The new scale maintains 20 grades. The minimum basic salary for the 20th grade will increase from Tk 8,250 to Tk 20,000, while the maximum for the 1st grade will rise from Tk 78,000 to Tk 156,000.

The full basic salary will be implemented in three phases between July 1, 2026, and July 1, 2027. This includes 40% of the increased basic salary from July 2026, 30% in January 2027, and the remaining 30% in July 2027. Various allowances will become effective from January 1, 2028.

Pensioners will also benefit from the phased implementation. Pension increases range from 55% to 100% depending on the current pension amount, with those receiving Tk 9,000 or less seeing a 100% rise.

The government plans to introduce a "One Grade One Pension" system gradually by 2030, acknowledging the significant financial pressure it would create if implemented immediately. This current structure serves as an alternative in the interim.

New benefits include a disability allowance of Tk 3,000 per month for government employees' special needs children. Additionally, mobile allowances, previously limited to Grade 5 and above, will now be applicable for all grades, considering internet and digital communication costs.

The new pay scale will benefit approximately 2.4 million military and civilian employees, along with 9.25 lakh retired employees and other eligible beneficiaries, totaling 3.3 million people. The annual additional cost to the government is estimated at Tk 1.05 trillion, with funds already allocated in the medium-term budget framework.

headline_marked: [[3 Air Force personnel die]] as pickup plunges from Dhaka airport's Third Terminal flyover
headline: 3 Air Force personnel die as pickup plunges from Dhaka airport's Third Terminal flyover
summary: Three Bangladesh Air Force members were killed and four others injured when their pickup truck lost control and fell from a flyover at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport's Third Terminal.
details: Three Bangladesh Air Force members were killed and four others injured when a pickup truck lost control and plunged from the second-story flyover of Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport's Third Terminal. The tragic incident occurred around 10:20 PM on Monday, August 31.

The Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) confirmed the fatalities and injuries in a statement. The deceased Air Force members have been identified as Warrant Officer Mahmud, Corporal Pias, and LAC Zubaidul.

Following the accident, the injured members were immediately transferred to Combined Military Hospital (CMH) in Dhaka for necessary medical treatment. Arrangements are also being made for the post-mortem procedures of the deceased.
